subject: strategy
text: - Telemetry is the `tracing` crate's event macros and, in escher-driver, two span macros (`info_span!`, `command` and, since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface, `tool_call`, §4), in the engine and upstream crates compiled in only with the `tracing` cargo feature (packages/blitz-dom/src/util.rs:26-27; packages/blitz-dom/src/events/ime.rs:27-28); escher-telemetry depends on `tracing` with no feature and always compiles its startup and panic events into the two native binaries of the seven_guis package, `seven_guis_native` and `escher-session`, whose engine `tracing` features stay off in a package-alone build (`-p seven_guis`; a workspace-wide build turns blitz-dom's on — Feature wiring, below); escher-driver is the second escher crate to take `tracing` ungated (`{ workspace = true }`, no `[features]` table; the workspace requirement is 0.1.40, the lock holds 0.1.44): its command span is compiled into both binaries through `seven_guis → escher-driver`; since 2026-10-10-driver-cli it is reached in `escher-session` by every call its host role runs — one closed span per hosted call — and since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface by its `mcp` role, where each `tools/call` writes one closed `tool_call` span and every instance verb run through `Session::run` adds its `command` child — and still by no code path in the windowed `seven_guis_native` (packages/escher-driver/src/mcp.rs:118-121; packages/escher-telemetry/Cargo.toml:13-16; packages/escher-telemetry/src/lib.rs:161; packages/escher-telemetry/src/panic.rs:11-21; packages/escher-driver/Cargo.toml:13-18; as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-07-driver-command-spans/report.md)

text: - By invocation: a build that resolves the whole workspace (`cargo test --workspace`, `ci-leg.sh fast`, CI's test leg) turns `blitz-dom/tracing` on — blitz's default `tracing` reaches blitz-shell and blitz-html, and each of those forwards to blitz-dom — while `cargo test -p blitz-tests` and a `-p seven_guis` build leave it off; so under the workspace build a test child that installs escher's sink at `info` also receives engine events: one `INFO blitz_dom::document … message=[redacted]` beside a driver `type` (packages/blitz-shell/Cargo.toml:21; packages/blitz-html/Cargo.toml:15; packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs:1902; as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-07-driver-command-spans/evidence/feature-unification.md, from cargo's resolved feature graph, the event at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-07-driver-command-spans/report.md; test-plan §9 → Engine features by runner). Measured at 2026-10-10-driver-cli for the session host: on a snapshot · click · type flow the workspace-built `escher-session` host prints that one engine line, `blitz_dom::document` at INFO, from `info` up and no further line at `debug` or `trace`, and the host built alone (`-p seven_guis`) prints none (as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-10-driver-cli/evidence/by-level.md); re-measured at 2026-10-14-stand-requirement-sweep on the same flow, the workspace-built host prints that engine line twice from `info` up — `trace` adding no line — and the host built alone still none (as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-14-stand-requirement-sweep/evidence/log-counts.md). Measured since 2026-10-14-quality-gates: the windowed `seven_guis_native`'s stderr by level as a workspace build makes it, on the host's display, with 0 needles (§8; as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-14-quality-gates/evidence/stderr-by-level.md)

subject: spans
text:
- `packages/escher-driver` — a second span, `tool_call`, since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface (answered by the founder, 2026-10-10, «Span с tool и ending», by question dialog in the overseer session, relayed verbatim by the overseer as his chosen option label; the English wording is the overseer's): built by hand with `tracing::info_span!(target: "escher_driver", "tool_call", tool = Empty, ending = Empty)`, opened and entered once per MCP `tools/call` request only — before its params are read — and held until its reply is written; two fields and no other, each a closed word: `tool`, the verb table's word — one of its twelve, `help` among them since 2026-10-12-self-description and `screenshot` since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot, and `lint` — unrecorded for an unknown tool, and `ending`, `accepted` · `refused` · `error` (a session error or a protocol error); an instance verb run through `Session::run` makes its `command` span the child by nesting — the executor unchanged — while the session verbs `start` · `status` · `stop` and, since 2026-10-12-self-description, `help`, answered by the server, leave a `tool_call` with no `command` child — a `help` call, held session or not, ending `accepted`, and an argument to it refused `malformed` by `validate_session`, ending `refused`; since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot a `screenshot` tool call ends `accepted` (its reply an `image` block then a `text` block) or `refused` (one text block, `isError` true) and parents its `command` child like every instance verb, measured in process in both layout modes (`stand_mcp_tools::a_screenshot_tool_call_answers_its_image_then_its_text_and_parents_its_command`, tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_mcp_tools.rs:631-704);
 a `lint` tool call ends `accepted` (its reply the JSON line `{"findings":[…]}`, one text block) or `refused` and parents one `command` child whose `verb` is `lint`, measured in process in both layout modes (`stand_mcp_tools::a_lint_tool_call_answers_the_readers_findings_and_parents_its_command`, tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_mcp_tools.rs:706-766); no field added, the span keeps its two; measured for `help` in process (`stand_mcp_tools::help_is_answered_by_the_server_and_parents_no_command`, tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_mcp_tools.rs:768-820, as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-12-self-description/report.md); an `advance` tool call, accepted on every session (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18), ends `accepted` and parents one `command` child whose `verb` is `advance` and which records no `cause` (tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_mcp_tools.rs:466-506); measured in process in both layout modes, one `tool_call` per call the parent of each `command` (`stand_mcp_tools`, its hand-written recorder; a mutation that leaves the span unentered turns it red) (packages/escher-driver/src/mcp.rs:118-121; packages/escher-driver/src/mcp.rs:179-213; tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_mcp_tools.rs:225-397; as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-10-mcp-surface/report.md)

subject: log-fields
text: - A closed span's line — a second record class since 2026-10-07-driver-command-spans, a boundary widening ratified by the founder (2026-10-09) as built — is written for each closed span whose target the allowlist admits, and no line when a span is created, recorded to, entered or exited: `{time} {LEVEL} {target} service.name=… service.version=… span={the span's name}`, then the span's own fields in the order recorded, then the layer's close fields `message`, `time.busy` and `time.idle`; level and target are the span's, the two timings are `tracing-subscriber`'s own (no escher code reads a clock for them), and `span` is a reserved field name; every pair, `span` included, passes the §8 scrub under the span's target; a string value is Debug-quoted (`span="command"`, `message="close"`), a number or a bool bare; a span from a target outside the allowlist writes no byte at any point; an event's line is unchanged, an event emitted inside a span included — it gains no span name and no span field; as read from a real capture: `… INFO escher_driver service.name=blitz-tests service.version=0.3.0-beta.2 span="command" verb="click" passes=1 settled=true added=1 removed=0 changed=1 message="close" time.busy=11.0ms time.idle=4.51µs` (packages/escher-telemetry/src/lib.rs:102-116; packages/escher-telemetry/src/format.rs:138-177; packages/escher-telemetry/src/format.rs:200-250; as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-07-driver-command-spans/report.md)

subject: log-fields
text: - The verdict fields: `task, client_exit, isolated, session_tools, client_version, model, tool_calls, server_tool_calls, wrong_calls, wrong_call_bar_pct, refused_calls, error_calls, spacer_calls, transcript_errors, counts_agree, lint_calls, screenshot_calls, advance_calls, part_reads, recorded_sessions, recording_kept, tasks_met, check_steps, check_expects, check_passed, check_can_fail, num_turns, duration_ms, cost_usd, input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens, transcript_file, outcome, reasons, ts` (`final_count` retired at 2026-10-15-cold-agent-test) — every one a count, a boolean or a closed word, no transcript text, tool argument, tool answer, reply or check; `counts_agree` ties the server's span lines to the transcript (the `tool_call` lines equal the escher tool uses, its refused + error lines the escher results marked `is_error`), `wrong_calls` = refused + error + foreign tool uses + permission denials, deciding the verdict against `wrong_call_bar_pct` (5), and the reasons add `capability-unused` (a counted verb or a part read unused), `recording-not-kept` and `wrong-calls-over-bar` (`wrong_calls × 100 > 5 × tool_calls`) after `task-unmet`, then `no-check`, `check-failed`, `check-cannot-fail` (scripts/cold-agent.sh:398-498; scripts/cold-agent.sh:161-175)
